prompts.step: approved sink and faucet orientation correction
prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the provided existing kitchen hero photograph for SURFORM. Make one localized functional orientation correction to the integrated island sink and faucet ONLY. The client explicitly says the cooktop STAYS EXACTLY where it is.
The camera looks from the living/dining side across the white island toward the rear kitchen counter and induction cooktop under the range hood. In the current image the integrated sink/faucet arrangement faces the living/dining side incorrectly. Reverse the functional orientation of the sink/faucet arrangement by 180 degrees ON THE SAME ISLAND so it is used from the working aisle between the island and the back counter, facing the cooktop.
Crucial geometry: keep the sink integrated in the same right-hand area of the white island. Mount the faucet on the NEAR / FOREGROUND / DINING-SIDE rim of the basin, rather than on the far rim where it is now. Its outlet points AWAY FROM THE CAMERA toward the inside of the bowl and the rear kitchen counter. The basin is BEHIND the faucet from our viewpoint, accessible to someone standing in the working aisle beside the cooktop. Correct the inner basin walls, smooth corner radii, perspective, rim and drain to match the new orientation naturally and credibly. Keep the drain correctly on the bowl floor, never embedded in a rim. Keep the chrome faucet height and modern square-arched design in realistic proportions. Leave the faucet OFF, with no water.
Do NOT swap sink and cooktop locations. The black induction cooktop must remain unchanged on the REAR countertop under the hood. Do NOT move the sink to the rear countertop. Do NOT move or redesign the island, kitchen cabinetry, hood, appliances or window.
Preserve everything else: the original camera, wide landscape framing, realistic daylight, shadows, graphite cabinets, light satin off-white solid-surface countertop, small folded cloth and ceramic bowl on the left, window and greenery on the right. Maintain natural photographic realism and construction plausibility, with no CGI gloss, no added text, no added people, no logo, no border. The output should look like the SAME photograph with only the sink/faucet corrected.

prompts.step: final instruction: remove only two cabinet door seams
prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit ONLY the supplied photograph. Remove ONLY the two thin vertical cabinet-door joint lines on the LONG FRONT GRAPHITE PANEL DIRECTLY UNDER THE SINK: one at approximately x=1100 from y=642 down to the bottom, and one at approximately x=1456 from y=594 down to the bottom (input is 1672 x 941).
Retouch those two hairline seams to match the surrounding graphite panel texture and natural shading. Nothing else.
IMPORTANT: KEEP the structural vertical corner at x≈585 below the island's left front corner. That edge separates the short side face and the long front face and is essential to the ORIGINAL PERSPECTIVE. KEEP the original short side face, original angled end, countertop shape, all edge profiles and geometry EXACTLY unchanged. Keep the thin shadow/reveal immediately under the countertop. The long front becomes continuous ONLY by erasing the two cabinet joints.
Preserve every other element exactly: same sink and faucet orientation, same cooktop, white countertop, all corners, other cabinetry, light above the cooktop, shadows, texture, camera and crop.
DO NOT add any lighting under the island. DO NOT round any corners. DO NOT redesign, change perspective, change colors or smooth away the structural end/corner. This is a tiny two-line retouch on the existing photograph, not a redesign. Same image dimensions.
